factor.name: Role separation: upgrade ≠ fee ≠ oracle
factor.scoring_methodology:
**What this measures**
This factor checks whether the upgrade, fee collection, and oracle configuration functions are assigned to distinct addresses or distinct multisigs — meaning no single address holds all three administrative powers simultaneously. The on-chain AccessControl or equivalent role mapping is queried for each of the three action types and compared for address overlap.

**Why it matters**
Role separation across upgrade, fee, and oracle functions prevents a single key compromise from granting an attacker total protocol control. An attacker who gains access to the oracle setter role should not also be able to upgrade the protocol or drain fee revenues. In practice, many DeFi protocols use a single deployer-controlled multisig for all three roles — which means that any compromise of that multisig constitutes a simultaneous oracle, fee, and upgrade authority breach. The evidence base shows that full-authority-concentration in a single key or multisig is strongly correlated with post-compromise total drains rather than partial impacts.

**Green / Yellow / Red**
Green is assigned when upgrade, fee, and oracle roles are held by three distinct addresses or multisigs with no overlap. Yellow covers two-of-three role separation (any one role shared with another). Red is assigned when all three roles are controlled by a single address or multisig, giving a single compromise total administrative authority.

**Common gray cases**
This factor is grayed when the protocol does not have all three role types (e.g., no oracle configuration because it uses an immutable oracle address — which is separately assessed under RD-F-180).

**Notable historical examples**
No cross-hacked incidents currently linked in database for this factor.

scored_protocols.evidence_summary: V2 fee/oracle/configurator role separation is partially documented, but this redo did not complete a current per-role owner extraction for every live V2 chain.

Upgrade role: Executor Lvl1/Lvl2. Fee/treasury: Collector (0x464C71f6c2F760DdA6093dCB91C24c39e5d6e18c, separate). Oracle config: AaveOracle managed via AIP through Executor. All three role types held by distinct contracts.

scored_protocols.evidence_detail: No evidence supports red; yellow records incomplete role mapping.
scored_protocols.evidence_summary: V4 fee/oracle/reserve control roles are split across hub/spoke/control-plane components, but complete owner extraction remains a packet gap.

scored_protocols.evidence_detail: The HubPool owner can relay arbitrary SpokePool admin calldata and directly set protocol fee capture, bond, liveness, and the UMA identifier. Official repository documentation says the HubPool owner governs SpokePools cross-chain. The passed AcrossCo proposal and delayed ACX portal do not publicly establish a replacement or separation of these roles.
scored_protocols.evidence_summary: Upgrade, fee, and oracle/configuration authority remains concentrated in the HubPool-owner control path; the pending AcrossCo transition has not publicly separated those roles.

All role types (upgrade, fee parameters, oracle config) are governed by the same BABY governance module — no separate role holders. Oracle is not applicable (no price oracle in core protocol). Upgrade role = governance. Fee parameters changed via governance (Proposal #8 reduced unbonding fees). Role separation is structurally absent in a pure on-chain governance model without granular role contracts. Not a data gap — structural architecture of Cosmos SDK x/gov.

Centrifuge documents separate ProtocolGuardian and OpsGuardian responsibilities, but the reviewed public material does not establish the complete current assignment of upgrade, fee-collection, and oracle-configuration roles. Full three-way role separation is not assessed.
Upgrade, fee, oracle, and pause roles are nominally separated, but related operational Safes retain broad manager/admin parameter authority.
